native_requalification.boundary: Single actual Core CLI refusal/MCP acknowledged stop, stale acknowledgement rejection/fresh retry, retained SQL row after normal resume over verify-full TLS, original OpenBao manager and credentials, persistent data/network and running sibling preservation. In-memory MCP through shipped handler; no Core HTTP/OIDC/browser or final ecosystem qualification. All unrelated gates skipped.

implemented: Reuse existing parser and state-file lock; no additional registry, revision store or resolution.
Target creation, existing empty-Target deletion and recovery-reference mutation capture protected original bytes and use SaveExpected.

Same-size/restored-time changes, concurrent unrelated Target additions, hardlinks/symlinks, legacy .tmp substitution, held-lock retry, empty versus absent owner and last pre-rename validation are tested.
Canonical native ownership and configuration ownership use one platform metadata authority; Unix UID/mode/link requirements preserved.
limitations: Populated Target detach/recovery remains unimplemented and mandatory.
Normal legacy Config.Save serializes but has no caller snapshot lease; only migrated mutation callers use SaveExpected.
Windows compile success is not Windows native ACL/lifecycle qualification; whole Windows CLI compatibility is not claimed.
All-consumer function, validity, continuity, Core destruction, supported handoff and final pinned ecosystem acceptance remain mandatory.
